paragraphs: What is worth experiencing is researching routes, organising transport and accommodation, explaining arrangements and looking after group members' needs. Liking travel does not equal liking coordinating services, tracking numbers and handling changes.

First distinguish itinerary organisation, on-site guiding, running a travel agency and specialised outdoor services. In China a guide certificate and a travel agency licence serve different purposes, and a paper exercise cannot create practice authority.

In O*NET39-7012.00, travel guides cover the planning, organisation and execution of long-distance travel, tourism and expeditions. Chinese national escorts, tour leaders and operations staff have overlapping tasks, and their legal status must be checked separately.

Use the fictional 12-person itinerary on this page to produce three timetables: the first version, the vehicle delay F1 and the venue early closure F2. Paper calculation and communication drafts only, with no real tour leading, driving, first aid or outdoor action.
What kind of person suits a travel guide?

Observe whether you can check times and service conditions, explain clearly to group members and, when facing a delay, keep the known facts and propose verifiable options. Organisation, service and accurate records need to be verified together.

This is an editorially designed career exploration, not a recruitment examination, a real travel recommendation or professional safety training. One successful schedule does not prove tour-leading or operating qualifications.

Positive signals are proactively asking about departure meeting points, journey times, opening hours and group members' needs and separating confirmed from unconfirmed arrangements; being willing to hear feedback and recalculate the impact.

Signals for caution are chasing only fun and a high price, ignoring group members' needs, meeting times or weather changes, changing the itinerary unilaterally and promising unconfirmed services, or playing down risk to close a sale.

Compare the three timetables and the communication record and explain why an option was kept, adjusted or suspended; then judge whether you are willing to keep doing route checking, service coordination and repeated confirmation.

United States 39-7012.00 travel guides plan, organise and execute long-distance travel, tourism and expeditions for individuals or groups. Related Chinese posts overlap in tasks, but the United States classification cannot be treated directly as a Chinese legal status.

Inputs are dates, routes, numbers, service bookings, transport and accommodation, equipment and group members' special needs. Opening hours and supplier status must be checked, and a promotional itinerary cannot replace a confirmed execution arrangement.

The editorial suggestion is to list the travel, activity and buffer time for each leg first, then check the key constraints and pending items; unknown information is not filled in as zero and personal experience is not passed off as verified conditions.

Outputs include the itinerary, service and equipment checks, group communication, anomaly handling and feedback records. A feasible option only means the paper conditions are met, not that transport and accommodation are confirmed or that real safety is assured.

Itinerary organisation focuses on routes and service coordination; accompanying a group focuses on delivering the arrangements, group members' needs and changes. O*NET also includes specialised expedition tasks requiring additional ability and local authority, which does not mean every post performs them.

Work with group members, the travel agency, operations staff, transport and accommodation and other service providers. Drivers, medical personnel and specialist instructors each carry their own responsibility, and a travel guide cannot replace their qualifications by virtue of the job title.

The typical BLS entry education for the combined occupation is high school equivalency plus on-the-job training; the Chinese historical samples separately list a bachelor's or college diploma, a foreign language and guide certificate conditions. Employer requirements cannot be generalised into a uniform national education level.

At the end of the service, evaluate the arrangements and feed back to the organiser; record the problems and handling status and protect group members' material. The learning portfolio uses a fictional list only and collects no real documents, health or payment information.

Compare the two task lines within this occupation: itinerary organisation and accompanying a group. The flow below is an editorial summary, and real execution follows the contract, service confirmation and institutional authority.

Check requirements → research routes → schedule times and services → check transport and accommodation → note items awaiting confirmation → hand over for execution

How do itinerary organisation and group accompaniment differ?

The organisation line turns routes and services into an executable plan; the execution line delivers the arrangements on a real trip, responds to group members and handles changes. A post may combine both, and the division of work must be checked with the institution and the project.
Core purpose
Arrange services according to the route, times and group members' needs and identify unconfirmed conditions.
On the trip, coordinate the agreed services, explain the arrangements and respond to group members' needs.
Main object and basis
Client requirements, route material, opening hours, transport and accommodation and service confirmations.
The contract and itinerary, meeting information, group members' needs, supplier replies and on-site status.
Core process
Check conditions, plan routes, coordinate services, recalculate times and hand over.
Check the meeting, explain the arrangements, follow up activities and changes, coordinate and record.
Main outputs
The itinerary and service list, the key constraints and the items awaiting confirmation.
Execution status, problem-handling handover and service evaluation.
Accountable party
The organisation operates under licence, the post coordinates within its authority and suppliers perform under contract.
Guides and tour leaders act under the applicable status and assignment; driving, medical care and specialist instruction carry separate duties.
Mode of coordination
Check times, numbers and conditions with operations staff, transport and accommodation and other service providers.
Explain and confirm with group members and service providers and report anomalies to the organiser promptly.
Delivery boundary
A paper itinerary cannot guarantee availability, weather or real safety.
Service coordination must not stand in for driving, first aid or specialist qualifications; Chinese guides and tour leaders must not take on business privately.
Key occupational judgements

The following is an editorially designed work self-check: check the route and times first, then examine the services, group members' needs and change responsibility, and do not treat a scheduling result as a professional safety decision.
Are the numbers, meeting point, dates and end times clear?
Are travel, activity, rest and unknown times separated?
Are the bookings and services confirmed, or still being requested?
After a vehicle delay or a changed closing time, which sections must be rescheduled?

Keep the original version, change only the conditions the feedback makes explicit and recalculate arrival and end times; a feasible result must not be manufactured by shortening the activity fixed in the prompt or ignoring the delay.
Do on-site service, taking payment or material handling exceed your authority?

Confirm under institutional process, the contract and the applicable jurisdiction; real health or location material is processed only as necessary and protected, and the learning exercise uses no real person's sensitive information.
Who receives the execution status, problems and follow-up handling?
Planning | researching routes and itineraries | arrange tourist activities using destination and route knowledge and check opening hours and key constraints.
Coordination | transport, accommodation and equipment | contact service providers to confirm conditions and check equipment quantity and quality and specialist support arrangements.
Service | explaining arrangements and group members' needs | explain the meeting, activities and restrictions and respond to special needs and questions.
Execution | following the itinerary and changes | deliver the confirmed arrangements, identify delays and service problems and coordinate and report within authority.
Records | costs and service feedback | keep the applicable accounts and confirmation records, evaluate the service and feed back to the organiser.

Specialised | checking ability and licensing | O*NET includes expedition, vehicle or first aid tasks; they are performed only in posts with the corresponding ability and authority and are not a general requirement.
Section heading | the work environment and working style of travel guides

The BLS combined occupation includes indoor and outdoor service, with standing and walking, part-time, seasonal and weekend and holiday schedules being fairly common. A travel guide may accompany a group for several days in a row; the specific schedule and rest are checked separately.

Common organisations and locations | travel arrangement service bodies, sightseeing transport, scenic areas and tourism activity organisers. Itinerary preparation may use telephone and email, while group accompaniment faces service locations and transport changes.

Work materials and tools | route material, itineraries, opening and service confirmations, equipment lists, email and spreadsheets. Familiarity with the tools does not mean holding driving, medical or operating authority.

Work organisation | distinguish the itinerary draft, the supplier confirmation and the actual execution status; hand unresolved matters to the corresponding post, and do not treat a recommendation or request as delivered.

Scheduling and workload | multi-day trips may have long working days with rest between legs, and the busy season may differ from the off season. At interview, check night contact, rest, transport and accommodation and extra costs.

Communication and coordination | explain changes and pending items to group members and check actual conditions with service providers; respect special needs and do not disclose health or location records.

Review and chain of responsibility | check meeting times, numbers, routes and service status and record the facts, the responsible person and the outcome for anomalies; personal guesswork cannot replace organisational confirmation.

Quality and occupational requirements | look at scheduling accuracy, clear communication, responding to needs and leaving a trail for anomalies. First compare preparation and execution within this occupation, then look at the outputs and responsibilities of management, accommodation, events and naturalist interpretation. Sharing clients or a venue does not make the occupations interchangeable.

It cannot be confirmed from the output alone. Check the route, each leg's time and the opening and service status; confirmations missing from the draft must stay pending, and an appearance of completeness cannot replace the basis for execution.
